---
title: Using the UI library
description: "The shared UI component library available to every app."
---

Every app builds its interface from `@lodekit/ui` — the **UI library**, part of the
shared toolchain. Import components like any package:

```ts
import { Badge, Button, Card, CardContent, Input } from "@lodekit/ui";
```

That line is from the Greenhouse showcase app, and it's the whole setup — no
installation, no copy-pasting component files, no configuration.

## One theme, one product

The components are [shadcn/ui](https://ui.shadcn.com/) — the same battle-tested set
used across the industry — carrying **one shared theme**. Colors, radii, spacing, and
typography come from theme tokens, not from each app's code. That's why a plant
tracker and an invoice tool built months apart look like two views of the same
product, and why restyling happens in one place instead of per app.

An app opts in with a single line in its `src/index.css`:

```css title="src/index.css"
@import "@lodekit/ui/theme.css";
```

In Greenhouse, that import is the entire file. It brings in the theme's tokens and
Tailwind setup, so utility classes and semantic colors like `text-muted-foreground`
and `text-destructive` work everywhere in the app.

Want different colors? Theming is yours, not the app's — you (or your agent) redefine
tokens in a plain CSS file, globally or per app, and every component follows. That's
covered in [Theming](/guide/theming/).

## What's in the box

The set is stock shadcn — Lodekit adds the theme, not custom component internals:

`accordion`, `alert`, `alert-dialog`, `aspect-ratio`, `avatar`, `badge`,
`breadcrumb`, `button`, `button-group`, `card`, `checkbox`, `collapsible`,
`combobox`, `command`, `context-menu`, `dialog`, `drawer`, `dropdown-menu`, `empty`,
`field`, `hover-card`, `input`, `input-group`, `input-otp`, `kbd`, `label`,
`menubar`, `navigation-menu`, `pagination`, `popover`, `progress`, `radio-group`,
`resizable`, `scroll-area`, `select`, `separator`, `sheet`, `sidebar`, `skeleton`,
`slider`, `sonner`, `spinner`, `switch`, `table`, `tabs`, `textarea`, `toggle`,
`toggle-group`, `tooltip`

— plus the `cn` helper for composing class names. Because the components are stock,
shadcn's own docs and examples apply directly; your agent already knows them well.

## See them under your theme

The best reference isn't a screenshot — it's the **UI catalog** running on your own
machine at `http://lodekit.localhost:7777/_ui/`. It renders every component above
under your live theme, so what you see there is exactly what your apps get, including
any theme overrides you've made.

## Composing with Tailwind

Components handle the pieces; Tailwind handles the arrangement. Layout, spacing, and
one-off tweaks are utility classes right on the components:

```tsx title="src/routes/index.tsx"
<Card>
  <CardContent className="flex gap-4 p-4">
    <img
      src={files.url(`cover-${id}`)}
      alt={`${plant.name}'s portrait`}
      className="h-24 w-32 rounded-md object-cover"
    />
    <div className="min-w-0 space-y-1">
      <p className="text-sm text-muted-foreground">{plant.species}</p>
      {snoozed && <Badge variant="secondary">😴 snoozed</Badge>}
    </div>
  </CardContent>
</Card>
```

That's the whole building picture: the stack, the anatomy, the data flow, the live
updates, and the components. For every handle and signature in one place, head to the
[SDK reference](/sdk/overview/).
